title: CROSSWIRE-1 subcase (i) responses->messages: qwen3.8-27b (responses wire, reasoning items) -> ACP switch -> claude-sonnet-5 (messages wire) -> 1 turn. The post-switch /v1/messages request replays the foreign qwen history; R8 PREEMPTIVE model-identity suppression must strip the foreign (qwen-identity) thinking blocks. Tolerant verdict (rt-xreplay1 discipline): the acceptance outcome is the FINDING — 200 (R8 sufficed, zero reactive-strip involvement) OR 400->strip+retry->200 (R8 missed something and the CROSSWIRE-1 reactive strip recovered). Both PASS; a retry storm (>=3 messages requests) or an unrecovered acp_error FAILs as a defect.

ndjson.label: TURN COMPLETES: the post-switch messages turn did not die (200 directly, or 400 recovered by the reactive strip).

wire.label: CONTROL (anti-vacuous pin): a pre-switch qwen request carried a reasoning INPUT item — real foreign reasoning exists to cross the wire. Without this the R8-suppression pin is vacuous.

R8 PREEMPTIVE (the messages-side net): the LAST post-switch messages request (nth=0 = newest claude request — the only request in the R8-sufficient branch, the strip-recovery request in the 400 branch; a static nth cannot express 'first-of-N' with N in {1,2}) carries NO thinking block. If a thinking block is present here, either R8 missed the foreign origin AND the upstream accepted it (1-request 200: the MSGTHINK-1 finding shape — a designed FAIL) or the strip did not mutate the re-sent request (2-request: a fix defect).

NO RETRY STORM: 1 messages request = R8 sufficed (200, zero reactive-strip involvement); 2 = R8 missed and the CROSSWIRE-1 reactive strip fired once (400->strip->200). >=3 = same-payload retry storm (the COMP-3 wart shape) or a strip loop -> defect.
POST-SWITCH ACCEPTED: the final messages request (R8-sufficient, or the reactive-strip recovery) reached 200.

CROSSWIRE-1 (i) VERDICT RECORD: last-captured wire response status line, verbatim (the recovered/accepted 200). The R8-sufficient vs reactive-strip finding is read from the count assert (1 vs 2) and the wire. recon op — always records, never fails.
